findings.title: Members tab toggle remounts the tab navigation
findings.problem:
SettingsLayout's content is `
{tabContent}
` on the Members tab and the bare `tabContent` fragment on every other tab. Overview, members, budgets and integrations routes all render the same ProjectDetailsPage instance (router.tsx), so switching between Members and another tab changes the element type at the content root (div vs Fragment) and React unmounts and remounts the whole subtree, including ProjectDetailsNavigation.
findings.impact: Every switch into or out of the Members tab destroys and recreates the tablist: the tab button the user just activated with the keyboard loses focus (focus drops to the document body, so the next Tab restarts from the top of the page), and the horizontally scrollable tablist (`overflow-x-auto`) resets its scroll position on narrow widths. This is an accessibility/lifecycle regression introduced by this change; other tab switches keep the nav mounted.
findings.recommendation:
Keep the content root element type stable across tabs, e.g. always render `
{tabContent}
` (or apply the bounded classes to a wrapper that exists on every tab), so ProjectDetailsNavigation is reconciled rather than remounted when the active tab crosses the Members boundary. Add a test asserting the nav node (or focus on the activated tab) survives a members <-> overview switch.
